title: January 6 Citizen Analysis Record
purpose: A structured civic-analysis layer for evaluating major January 6 questions without converting political interpretation into fact.
method: Identify the claim or competing claims.
Separate court holdings from allegations and political judgments.
Separate government findings from judicial findings.
Identify material facts that remain disputed or unresolved.
Match the level of certainty to the strength of the record.

questions.question: Did the 2020 election challenges establish a legal basis to change the presidential outcome?
questions.discipline: Distinguish procedural dispositions from merits rulings and preserve the certified Electoral College result as the official outcome.

questions.question: What authority did the Vice President have on January 6?
questions.discipline: Distinguish the constitutional and statutory framework in force in 2021 from later statutory reforms.

questions.question: What caused the breach of the U.S. Capitol?
questions.discipline: Use synchronized chronology and direct evidence; sequence alone does not prove causation.

questions.question: What responsibility did President Donald Trump bear?
questions.discipline: Keep political judgment, congressional findings, criminal allegations and judicial holdings distinct.

questions.question: Did federal and local agencies have sufficient warning?
questions.discipline: Compare information actually available before January 6 with later oversight findings.

questions.question: Why was the Capitol not better protected?
questions.discipline: Separate planning, intelligence, staffing, command and mutual-aid questions from hindsight.

questions.question: Was the National Guard response unnecessarily delayed?
questions.discipline: Separate request, authorization, mission approval, mobilization, deployment and arrival times.

questions.question: How should congressional objections to electoral votes be understood?
questions.discipline: Distinguish the lawful congressional objection process from violence or unlawful entry.

questions.question: How should competing elector documents be understood?
questions.discipline: Compare each document, representation and participant's conduct rather than applying a single characterization without examining the facts.

questions.question: Were January 6 defendants treated fairly?
questions.discipline: Evaluate defendants by individual conduct, charge, disposition, sentence, appeal and later legal developments.

questions.question: What did later Supreme Court decisions actually change?
questions.discipline: Apply each holding only to the legal question the Court actually decided.

questions.question: How should later executive clemency be understood?
questions.discipline: Preserve the historical charge, plea, verdict and sentence while separately recording later clemency.

questions.question: What do the pipe-bomb investigation and later developments establish?
questions.discipline: Treat this as a separate evidence file and do not infer relationships unsupported by authenticated evidence.

questions.question: What should America learn from January 6?
questions.discipline: Separate normative civic lessons from historical factual findings and identify the evidence supporting each premise.

privacy: Any future interactive citizen assessment should be private by default and should not be used to construct a political profile.
